newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends flat, securities stay firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends flat, securities stay firm.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday unchanged at 0.05-0.25 percent and dealers said they expected call money to remain easy next week.
"There were no deals today as it is the reporting day," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Four-day money was quoted in the 1.5-2.5 percent range but it is not clear whether any trades were done."
Another dealer said opening rates for call money on Saturday would depend on the results of a repo auction to be held later on Friday.
"I do not see rates rising very much even if there is a good response to the repo auction," he said. "Probabaly rates may open around 2.0-3.0 percent."
Dealers said prices of governemnt securities remained firm in moderate trade. Trade volumes dropped to 3.33 billion rupees from Thursday's 5.5, they said.

"The focus was largely on short and medium-maturity securties today," said a money market dealer. "Prices continued to be firm as easy liquidity and expectations of low interest rates in future led to buying interest."

The Reserve Bank of India releases its credit and monetary policy for the first half of 1997/98 (April-March) on April 15 amid widespread expectations that it will announces measures leading to a fall in interest rates.
